title: The daemon itself
description: Routes that describe this process rather than the work it carries.

SchedulerPulse.description: What the clock says about its own last pass. A pass that fired nothing and a scheduler that stopped are both silence from outside, so the clock reports itself the way a scan does.

at.description: When the last pass ran. Absent means no pass has finished yet, which is the ordinary state for the first tick after startup.

due.description: How many came due on this pass. Separate from `fired` because a due schedule whose dispatch was refused is not the same as nothing being due.

note.description: Why a pass did nothing, when the reason was not that nothing was due.

Health.description: GET /v1/health, open without a token: that this daemon is alive and which implementation it is, and nothing else. No path, no port, nothing about the work; those are in Diagnostics.

reason.description: Why `ok` is false, when it is. Absent when ok. The name only: what is behind it is in Diagnostics.

served_by.description: Which implementation answered. This is how a reader tells the Go daemon from the Swift app on the same port.

Diagnostics.description: GET /v1/diagnostics, this machine's own token only (a paired device is 403): what health used to carry about the process — its state directory, its ports, the clock's last pass and the broker's own account of itself.

ProposalDiagnostics.description: /v1/diagnostics.proposals (design-decisions T4, board-redesign §4.4): what the server decided about asking a person in the conversation, and what the sessions reported doing, counted from the proposals table — durable, the same after a restart. `ask_true` is the proposals the server let be asked; `asked_inline` the ones a session reported asking; `asked_inline_unprompted` those of them the server had said not to ask, which is a briefing not followed. `matched` is `asked_inline == ask_true` with none unprompted; an ask a session has not reported yet also reads as unmatched.

pending.description: Proposals waiting for an answer: the "to confirm" area and the ones asked in a conversation.

oldest_pending_at.description: When the proposal waiting longest was made. Absent when none waits.

error.description: The counts could not be read; every number beside it is zero and means nothing.

HealthReason.description: Why /v1/health says ok:false. `broker_beat_stalled`: the broker's loop has not finished a pass in more than three ticks. `capacity_exhausted`: an evidence or security-audit row of the capacity register is full with nothing making room, or its last write failed (docs/limits.md §4.5). `capacity_beat_stalled`: the loop that measures the register has not finished a pass in more than three ticks, so nothing is watching whether anything is full. `work_sweep_stalled`: the board's sweep has not finished a pass in more than three ticks, so a landing or a delivery would not move the board (design-decisions T3). When two hold, the first in this list is given.

CapacityDiagnostics.description: /v1/diagnostics.capacity: every row of the capacity register (internal/domain/capacity) as the last pass of its beat read it. Each row answers the four questions: its limit, what happens when it is full, who is told, and who decides what is let go (docs/limits.md §4.1, design-guidelines DG-2).

counting_since.description: When this process began counting. Every counter on a row counts from here unless the row says `counters_durable`.

override_problems.description: Parts of CLAWDLINE_NEXT_CAPACITY this process refused — an override that would raise a limit, name no row, or not read as one. The default stood for each.

CapacityBeat.description: The loop that measures the register. It is observable because a loop that stopped and a loop with nothing to say are the same silence from outside (DG-1).

at.description: When the last pass finished. Absent before the first.

event_errors.description: Events this beat could not write to the store.

running.description: Whether this process started the beat. A daemon that did not has every row `unknown`.

stalled.description: No pass has finished in more than three ticks.

CapacityEntry.description: One row of the capacity register.

at_limit.description: What happens today when the row is full.

coalesced.description: Newer values that replaced a waiting one on a latest-value buffer. Nothing was lost: a reader was told once where it would have been told twice.

counters_durable.description: The counters survive a restart: the row's own store keeps them.

deviation.description: Present when `at_limit` is not what the row's class requires: what it requires, and which decision brings it.

disconnected.description: Readers the row ended because they were not keeping up, each to come back and read afresh.

disk_free_bytes.description: Free space on the disk the row is on, when it is a file and that could be read.

dropped.description: Things that reached nobody: on a buffer, what was let go without the other side hearing of it.

error.description: Why the row could not be measured, when `state` is unknown.

evicted_by.description: Who decides what the full row lets go of.

exhausted.description: The fact /v1/health turns on: an evidence or security-audit row, full with nothing making room, or failing to write.

failing.description: The last write to the row, or its last at-limit action, failed.

growth_per_day.description: Growth over this process's samples, at least an hour of them, on a row that projects.

last_action_at.description: When the row last refused, evicted, rotated, dropped, coalesced or disconnected something.

limit.description: The limit this process runs the row at, in `unit`.

note.description: Anything a reader should know about a reading that is not an error.

notices.description: Notification intents this row produced: a `capacity.notify` event on entering critical or full and on recovering, at most one a day.

notices_suppressed.description: Notices the one-a-day rule held back.

projected_full_at.description: When the row reaches its limit at `growth_per_day`. Two weeks before, the row is warn whatever its ratio.

ratio.description: used / limit. Null when the row could not be measured, which is not zero.

told.description: The channels a full row reaches.

used.description: How much the row holds, in `unit`. Null when it could not be measured, which is not zero.

write_errors.description: Writes to the row that failed. On store.db, writes the database refused for a storage reason (full, read-only, I/O, corrupt); a busy or conflicting writer is not one.

CapacityClass.description: What kind of data a row holds; it decides which at-limit behaviours are allowed (docs/limits.md §4.2).

CapacityAction.description: `none`: nothing is refused, removed or rotated; the limit is only reported. No class allows it, so a row that does it has a `deviation`.

CapacityState.description: ok below warn_at, warn below 95%, critical below 100%, full at or past it. Going down needs five points under a threshold. unknown: the row could not be measured, which is not ok.

CapacityChannel.description: diagnostics: this route, always. health: /v1/health says capacity_exhausted, never the name or the numbers. notice: a capacity.notify event, a push once C4 wires it. cloud_status: /v1/cloud/status. log: the daemon's log. sender: whoever sent what the row turned away, in the answer to that request.

CapacityDecider.description: person: the daemon lets nothing go; only a person removes it. daemon: the daemon lets go by the rule in at_limit.

InventorySession.description: A raw row of the terminal reading, before the fleet list drops the rows that are not assistants.
